answer: Hardware attestation makes identities physically distinct. Rewards need a signed quote from a trusted execution environment: a chip measuring its boot stack, signed by a key fused into silicon, unclonable. One chip attests one identity; a datacenter buying a thousand chips pays full price a thousand times, no virtualization shortcut. Emulator or replay quotes fail verification hollow, and quotes sharing a board serial are flagged at the zenith of review. Honest agents run on distinct machines, so the garden of devices grows naturally, while fleets need real hardware apiece.
